That's half right, and the wrong half is costing you goals.

**What's true:** speed matters. A harder shot gives the keeper less time to react, and research on penalties finds that reaction time is the keeper's main limit on shots aimed at the outer parts of the goal ([Tambusso et al.](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sebastian-Tambusso/publication/259968890_Taking_the_goalkeeper%27s_side_in_association_football_penalty_kicks/links/544903cd0cf2f14fb8145b32/Taking-the-goalkeepers-side-in-association-football-penalty-kicks.pdf)).

**What's not true:** that placement doesn't matter. The same study found that in the central part of the goal, saves were statistically independent of ball speed and reaction time. A hard shot down the middle can still be saved, because the keeper doesn't have to move to stop it. Speed only beats the keeper when the ball is also aimed where they have to dive. And a shot that sails over the bar scores nothing at any speed.

Your notes show this directly. You plant too far behind the ball to get a longer swing, and that lifts the ball over the bar. So chasing maximum power is the reason some of your shots miss.

**Worked example:** two penalties.
- A: full power, 5 cm below the crossbar, but it clears the bar. It's a miss.
- B: about 80% power, placed 30 cm inside the post. The keeper's reaction time is at least about 0.7 s ([The penalty in football](https://lida.sport-iat.de/dfb/Record/4017215?lng=en)), so a well-placed ball at that pace is usually out of reach.

B scores. Your mission is to place the ball in the corner *with* power, and that means accuracy first and then as much pace as you can keep while still hitting the spot.

I only ran one search and didn't read the studies' full texts, so treat the details as a general picture.

Quick check: if you plant your foot level with the ball, what do you expect to happen to the ball's height, and why might that help your placement?

I can also write a short lesson on how plant-foot position, striking surface and contact point trade power against accuracy, if you want one.

Sources:
- [Taking the goalkeeper's side in association football penalty kicks](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sebastian-Tambusso/publication/259968890_Taking_the_goalkeeper%27s_side_in_association_football_penalty_kicks/links/544903cd0cf2f14fb8145b32/Taking-the-goalkeepers-side-in-association-football-penalty-kicks.pdf)
- [The penalty in football](https://lida.sport-iat.de/dfb/Record/4017215?lng=en)
